If it was done as a mini-series, a series of movies, or just one long supermovie, what are some of the roles you'd cast?
(x-post /v/Movies) I know it's already been attempted a few times, but who would you cast in a (good) film adaptation of The Count of Monte Cristo?

I'd love to see Benedict Cumberbatch attempt the role of the Count. He's young enough to play a good Dantes, but has the stage presence and commanding voice that I attribute to the Count. Villefort has always been the most intellectual of Dantes' adversaries, so I'd be interested in seeing Mads Mikkelsen in that role. He's got the calculating coolness I expect from Villefort, and I think that would play well against Cumberbatch's Count.

A few minor roles I'd like to fill would start with Jeremy Irons as Noirtier. He'd fit the fatherly, cheerful, Jacobin air that Noirtier has, and it would create an interesting dynamic with Mikkelsen's somber Villefort, similar to their relationship in the book.

I'm not sure who I'd cast for Danglars or Fernand, but I'd pick Steve Carell for Caderousse. He can portray that sense of cheerful self interest that Caderousse varies around with him.

A faithful movie or series about the book would be fairly challenging, but I think any decent actor could play any of the roles.

I'm sick of the same actors in every movie. Get a bunch of actors that most people aren't familiar with. Maybe a few more well knowns for the title roles, but they have to fit.

I don't think an actor from a different kind of genre would be a good fit. Steve Carell as suggested by ChillyHellion. I don't think that's a good fit. He's a comedy actor.

I can respect that perspective. I'm just curious if anyone has anyone specific in mind when they think about a film adaptation. To be honest I think it's too long a story for a movie, and that's part of the reason the most recent (2002) attempt was so bad. I think a miniseries could follow the books closely and do fine. There was a French language miniseries (1998), but that one also made too many changes to the plot, many of them strikingly unnecessary. The casting in that miniseries was very good.

Edit: and okay, maybe no Carell for Caderousse, but I'm sticking with the rest of them. I think the problem with The Count himself is that you have to have an actor that can play a convincing Dantes, who is uneducated, simple, and honest, but who can also play the role of the Count, a man who is 14 years older, experienced, ruthless, sophisticated, and with a commanding presence that's totally divorced from Dantes' character.

Gerard Depardieu was an excellent Count, but they had to get a different actor to play Dantes, and explained the difference as being 18 years in age and tried to show as little of Dantes as possible, telling most of the story from the Count's perspective.

Jim Caviezel did a good job as Dantes in the 2002 film, but his Count of Monte Cristo always came across as a young man pretending to be someone else, and he just lacked the commanding presence that the Count requires. It's a tricky role to balance, which is what makes it interesting.

I agree with you. I only mentioned Carell because he seemed out of place with the rest of what you've said. Caderousse wasn't a joker, he was a greedy, lying piece of shit.

I think Adrien Brody as the count would do well. He has the "dark features" that are mentioned in the book so much. I'm sure it's to do with his melancholy and desire for revenge driving everything he does, but I think that would come across well for him in that role.

I'm simply not a Benedict Cumberbatch fan, and I can't even really tell you why. I don't hate the guy, he's just not my preferred go to for anything (except maybe dragons voices - His Smaug was excellent).

I that's understandable; there are plenty of actors that just rub me the wrong way without having a good reason why. Adrien Brody is a choice I hadn't thought of, but I think he would fit the role well. He has that kind of inaccessible air that makes him difficult to read when he wants to be, which is another of the Count's traits.

One thing I've always found interesting about the book is that the initial story is told from the perspective of Edmond Dantes; we get inside his head and we know his thoughts and feelings about each event. But when he returns as the Count of Monte Cristo, the story shifts and we don't ever get to see inside his head again. The rest of the story is told through the perspective of the people around him. I think Brody would do a good job with the role.

That's true, and I think being on the outside looking in was a great aspect, because you already know all his motivations, it's just the follow through that you're waiting for.
